description: Exception handling for burred parts at press-fit interface, with supplier corrective action and downstream trace.

box_1.text: Collect five parts with detected burrs. Inspect the burr location and orientation using a magnifier to determine whether it is at the insertion lead chamfer or on the cylindrical press fit surface.

box_2.text: Is the burr present on parts before they enter the assembly process (incoming material defect)?

box_3.text: Inspect parts from the supply conveyor input side before they reach the assembly station to confirm the burr is present in the incoming material.

box_4.text: Quarantine the current input batch. Create a non conformance record for the incoming material and notify the quality assurance team. Reload from a confirmed conforming batch.

box_5.text: Is the burr present on all processed parts or only on parts from a specific pressing cycle?

box_6.text: Run a slow test cycle and inspect parts at the press output for every five cycles to determine whether the burr pattern is consistent or linked to a specific machine phase.

box_7.text: If the burr correlates with a specific cycle phase, identify the tooling component responsible (pressing head edge, guide surface, or nest edge) and inspect it immediately.

box_8.text: Does the pressing head edge have an acceptable chamfer condition (no sharp edge or chipping)?

box_9.text: Inspect the pressing head leading edge under magnification for chipping, sharp transitions, or material build up that could be transferred to the part.

box_10.text: Replace the pressing head or have the edge repolished to the specified chamfer radius. Verify the edge condition before resuming.

box_11.text: Is the press guide alignment free of lateral offset (no side loading of the pressing head against the part)?

box_12.text: Check the lateral clearance of the pressing head in the guide bushing. Verify that the pressing head moves without radial contact against the guide wall during descent.

box_13.text: Realign the press guide bushing to eliminate lateral offset. Verify alignment with a test pressing cycle before resuming production.

box_14.text: Quarantine all affected parts and record the root cause and corrective action in the quality log. Notify quality assurance team with sample parts for disposition.

box_15.text: Is the root cause of the burr an incoming material defect requiring a supplier corrective action?

box_16.text: Complete the following steps: 1. Compile defect data for the affected batch: quantity, rejection rate, and spec limit. 2. Cross-reference rejections against the production schedule to identify the batch window. 3. Confirm whether any burred parts were released to downstream assembly.

box_17.text: Refer to the supplier corrective action request procedure.

box_18.text: Were any burred parts released to downstream assembly or shipped before detection?

box_19.text: Trace all parts from the burr fault window through downstream stations and customer delivery records. Quarantine any located parts.

box_20.text: Issue customer advisory notice if any burred parts reached shipment, notify quality assurance manager.

box_21.text: End, Customer advisory issued. quality assurance disposition and supplier CA monitoring required.

box_22.text: End, Notify quality assurance team and maintenance team. Procedure complete.
